PullRequest.Title: Copilot setup: read the Copilot page in order with screen readers
PullRequest.Body:

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#7531. Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10007 (from test plan item microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9852).

NVDA read the Windows setup's **GitHub Copilot CLI** page from the bottom up: the "Learn more" link first, then the options from last to first, and the question last.

Screen readers follow the window order of a page's controls. Each control `copilot.iss` creates was placed above the ones before it, so the window order was the reverse of the page. `CopilotAddText`, `CopilotAddOption` and `CopilotAddFooter` now call `SendToBack` right after setting `Parent`, so the window order matches the page. The Tab order doesn't depend on the window order and is unchanged.

### How to test
1. Start NVDA, run the User Installer, and go to the **GitHub Copilot CLI** page.
2. Press NVDA+B: NVDA reads the question, then the options from top to bottom, each followed by its description, then the license note with **Learn more**.

### Validation
- Stub user installer, reading the page's child windows in window order, before and after:
  - before: link, "Don't add" description, "Don't add" option, ..., "Install now" option, question (reversed);
  - after: question, "Install now" option and description, "when I first run" option and description, "Don't add" option and description, link (passed).
- Tab order after the change, from the selected option: Learn more, Back, Next (unchanged; passed).
- ISCC compile of the user and system x64 installers with the Copilot shim: passed.
- Installer Pascal harness: 90 of 90 passed.
- Not run: NVDA itself.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Windows installer advances from task selection to the GitHub Copilot CLI choice page (basic or full variant).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NextButtonClick waits for the existing Copilot probe, then CopilotPreparePage constructs exactly one selected page before navigation can continue. The added SendToBack calls run synchronously during that one-time construction, but only for a fixed 6 controls on the basic page or 8 controls on the full page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract the bundled Copilot shim to the temporary directory and poll/read the probe result INI file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction at most, one result read, and polling every 50 ms for up to 6 seconds; guarded by CopilotShimExtracted and CopilotProbeRead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shim extraction, result-file polling, and INI reads occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The result wait precedes page construction and may block advancing from task selection; the added z-order calls execute only after this existing wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch copilot.exe --vscode-shim probe once without waiting directly on Exec.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one probe process per installer run, guarded by CopilotProbeStarted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single probe subprocess was launched before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The process runs ahead where possible, but NextButtonClick can wait for its result for up to 6 seconds before preparing the page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The user-installer probe may check Copilot CLI download availability; the system installer explicitly passes --no-network.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one network-capable user-scope probe per installer run; no per-control or per-page fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same user-scope probe could access the network before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Its probe result can be on the page-navigation critical path, but the diff neither introduces nor reschedules it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Control count is compile-time bounded: 6 controls for the basic page and 8 for the full page. Only one page variant is built after the probe determines CopilotPageKind, so the added work does not scale with files, repositories, history, user data, or repeated navigation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All page construction and z-order updates are serialized on the installer UI thread. The probe subprocess is launched asynchronously but is explicitly awaited before page construction; the diff does not change its concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Probe launch/read and page construction are positively cached with CopilotProbeStarted, CopilotProbeRead, CopilotBasicPageBuilt, and CopilotFullPageBuilt. Returning through the wizard does not repeat SendToBack or the boundary work. There is no collection-dependent cache key or negative-cache change in the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and cardinality: every added call is inside one-time builder helpers, all call sites and builder guards were inspected, and only one page variant is selected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact native cost of each SendToBack call is not measured, but its invocation count and lifecycle are fully bounded and tiny; no realistic scaling trigger is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff adds a fixed 6–8 native z-order operations during one-time page setup, with no new expensive boundary, loop amplification, cache defeat, retained growth, or repeated render path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff hunks. Traced installer page construction, repeat-navigation guards, and the transitive probe subprocess/filesystem/network boundaries. The added z-order updates are fixed-cardinality, one-time synchronous UI setup and do not establish a concrete performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
